title: 1967 AHSME Problem 10
statement:
If

\[ \begin{aligned} &\frac{a}{10^x-1}+\frac{b}{10^x+2}\\ &\qquad=\frac{2\cdot10^x+3} {(10^x-1)(10^x+2)} \end{aligned} \]

is an identity for positive rational values of \(x,\) then the value of \(a-b\) is:

solutions.text:
Clearing denominators gives \[ \begin{aligned} &a(10^x+2)+b(10^x-1)\\ &\qquad=2\cdot10^x+3. \end{aligned} \] Therefore \(a+b=2\) and \(2a-b=3.\) Solving gives \(a=\frac{5}{3},\ b=\frac{1}{3},\) so \(a-b=\frac{4}{3}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
